rules.title: App caches
rules.description: Cache folder named exactly after an installed app's bundle identifier. macOS designates ~/Library/Caches for data apps can recreate.
rules.regenerationImpact: The app recreates its cache; it may start more slowly once and re-download some content.
rules.evidence: Exact bundle-identifier folder of an installed, non-Apple app inside ~/Library/Caches.

rules.title: Google Chrome cache
rules.description: Chrome's per-profile web cache (not bookmarks, passwords or history, which live in Application Support).
rules.regenerationImpact: Web pages load from the network again; sites may be slower the first time.
rules.evidence: Documented Chrome cache location.

rules.title: Firefox cache
rules.description: Firefox's per-profile web cache (profiles themselves are in Application Support and are not touched).
rules.regenerationImpact: Web pages load from the network again.
rules.evidence: Documented Firefox cache location.

rules.title: Brave cache
rules.description: Brave's per-profile web cache.
rules.regenerationImpact: Web pages load from the network again.
rules.evidence: Documented Brave cache location.

rules.title: Microsoft Edge cache
rules.description: Edge's per-profile web cache.
rules.regenerationImpact: Web pages load from the network again.
rules.evidence: Documented Edge cache location.

rules.title: Slack caches
rules.description: Chromium cache folders inside Slack's data folder. Messages, sign-in and settings are not touched.
rules.regenerationImpact: Slack re-downloads images and recompiles scripts; first launch is slower.
rules.evidence: Standard Electron/Chromium cache folder names inside Slack's documented data folder.

rules.title: Visual Studio Code caches
rules.description: Chromium caches and cached extension downloads inside VS Code's data folder. Settings, extensions and backups are not touched.
rules.regenerationImpact: VS Code recompiles cached code on next launch; startup is slower once.
rules.evidence: Standard Electron cache folder names inside VS Code's documented data folder.

rules.title: Discord caches
rules.description: Chromium cache folders inside Discord's data folder.
rules.regenerationImpact: Discord re-downloads images and recompiles scripts.
rules.evidence: Standard Electron cache folder names inside Discord's documented data folder.

rules.title: Homebrew download cache
rules.description: Downloaded bottles and casks kept by Homebrew after installing.
rules.regenerationImpact: Homebrew downloads packages again if you reinstall them. Alternatively run `brew cleanup`.
rules.evidence: Homebrew's documented cache folder (`brew --cache`).

rules.title: pip cache
rules.description: Python package downloads cached by pip.
rules.regenerationImpact: pip downloads packages again when needed.
rules.evidence: pip's documented cache folder on macOS.

rules.title: Yarn cache
rules.description: Package archives cached by Yarn.
rules.regenerationImpact: Yarn downloads packages again when needed.
rules.evidence: Yarn's documented cache folder on macOS.

rules.title: CocoaPods cache
rules.description: Pod sources cached by CocoaPods.
rules.regenerationImpact: CocoaPods downloads pods again on the next install.
rules.evidence: CocoaPods' documented cache folder.

rules.title: npm cache
rules.description: npm's content-addressable package cache.
rules.regenerationImpact: npm downloads packages again; offline installs stop working until it does. npm's own command is `npm cache clean --force`.
rules.evidence: npm's documented cache folder (`npm config get cache`).

rules.title: Xcode DerivedData
rules.description: Build products and indexes Xcode creates for each project.
rules.regenerationImpact: The next build of each project is a full rebuild and re-index, which can take a long time.
rules.evidence: Xcode's default DerivedData location.

rules.title: Xcode device support files
rules.description: Debug symbols copied from devices you connected to Xcode.
rules.regenerationImpact: Xcode copies symbols again the next time you connect that device, which can take several minutes.
rules.evidence: Xcode's documented device support folders.

rules.title: Simulator caches
rules.description: Caches created by the iOS Simulator (not simulator devices or their data).
rules.regenerationImpact: Simulators rebuild their caches on next boot.
rules.evidence: CoreSimulator cache folder.

rules.title: Old app logs
rules.description: Log folders of installed apps with no changes for at least 30 days.
rules.regenerationImpact: Old logs are no longer available for troubleshooting.
rules.evidence: Exact bundle-identifier folder of an installed app in ~/Library/Logs, unchanged for 30 days.

rules.title: Old crash and diagnostic reports
rules.description: Crash and hang reports older than 30 days.
rules.regenerationImpact: These reports are no longer available to you or to developers you might send them to.
rules.evidence: macOS's per-user diagnostic report folder.

rules.title: Old downloaded installers
rules.description: Disk images and installer packages in Downloads that are older than 30 days.
rules.regenerationImpact: You would need to download the installer again.
rules.evidence: Installer file types directly in ~/Downloads.

rules.title: App caches (by app name)
rules.description: Cache folder named exactly like an installed app (for example Steam). macOS designates ~/Library/Caches for data apps can recreate.
rules.regenerationImpact: The app recreates its cache; it may start more slowly once and re-download some content.
rules.evidence: Folder in ~/Library/Caches named exactly like an installed, non-Apple app.

rules.title: Downloaded app updates
rules.description: Update packages an installed app downloaded with its updater (Squirrel “ShipIt”). They are only needed until the update is installed.
rules.regenerationImpact: The app downloads its next update again when one is available.
rules.evidence: Folder named after an installed app's bundle identifier followed by .ShipIt, the updater's download location.

rules.title: Firefox update downloads
rules.description: Firefox updates that were downloaded to be installed.
rules.regenerationImpact: Firefox downloads its next update again when one is available.
rules.evidence: Documented Firefox update download folder.

rules.title: Web caches of desktop apps
rules.description: Chromium cache folders inside the data folder of an installed app built with Electron. Sign-ins, settings and documents are not touched.
rules.regenerationImpact: The app re-downloads images and recompiles scripts; the first launch is slower.
rules.evidence: Standard Chromium cache folder names inside the data folder of an installed app that contains the Electron framework.

rules.title: Developer tool caches
rules.description: Download and build caches of command-line developer tools (node-gyp, Go, the VS Code C/C++ extension, Swift Package Manager, pnpm, TypeScript).
rules.regenerationImpact: Each tool downloads or rebuilds what it needs the next time it runs; the first build can be slower.
rules.evidence: Documented cache folders of these tools on macOS.

rules.title: Browser builds for automated tests
rules.description: Browsers that Playwright and Cypress downloaded to run automated tests.
rules.regenerationImpact: Install them again with `npx playwright install` or `npx cypress install`, which downloads several hundred megabytes.
rules.evidence: Documented download folders of Playwright and Cypress.
